prs.title: refactor(formatter): embed JS through `JsRoot` and `JsEmbeddedIn`
feat(formatter): format a template's expressions and handlers as `JsRoot`
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Adds what a Vue template needs to `format_to_ir`. Nothing uses it until #28848.

- `JsRoot::Expression`: an expression in the host's delimiters (`{{ a }}`, `:a="b"`)
  - Prints as is, in a group, or hugging the delimiters
  - Its root prints under the `Program` (`JsFormatContext::is_embedded_root`), so no statement rule (`;`, ASI guard) applies
- `ProgramSemicolons::MarksStatements`: a host that reads code holding a `;` as statements (Vue's `@click`)
  - Under `semi: false`, a `;` still joins the top-level statements, as an ASI guard for the host
  - A lone expression keeps or drops its `;` as written

The output reads to the host as the input does.
Where no print rule keeps that, `format_to_ir` returns `Err` and the host prints the code as written.

prs.title: feat(formatter_htmlish): format Vue templates
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Formats Vue files in `oxc_formatter_htmlish`. Nothing routes `.vue` here until #28848.

- SFC blocks print as blocks; `<script>` / `<style>` indent as `vueIndentScriptAndStyle` says
- A block that is no markup (`<i18n lang="json">`) formats in its language
- `{{ }}` and directive values are dispatched as JS (`JsInVueTemplate`), in the file's script language
- `v-for` is split as Vue reads it
- A value that does not format, and `v-pre` content, print as written

Policy: the output compiles with `@vue/compiler-sfc` as the input does (`crates/oxc_formatter_htmlish/AGENTS.md` "What Vue reads").

prs.title: feat(oxfmt)!: format `parser:vue` files by `oxc_formatter_htmlish`
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Fixes #28264

`.vue` files and `vue` code blocks no longer format through Prettier.

- Markup by `oxc_formatter_htmlish`, template JS by `oxc_formatter`
  - Adds `JsRoot::FunctionParams` / `JsRoot::TypeParameters` (`v-for`, `v-slot`, `<script generic>`)
  - `<style>` is also handled by `oxc_formatter_css`
- `prettier-plugin-oxfmt` now formats only Svelte and Astro scripts

⚠️ Breaking: the output differs from Prettier's where Prettier's compiles otherwise, each in `apps/oxfmt/DIVERGENCES.md`.

prs.title: fix(oxlint,oxfmt): resolve Vite+ config root from the config file directory
prs.author: fengmk2
prs.body:
In Vite+ mode, Oxlint and Oxfmt loaded `vite.config.*` with `resolveConfig({ configFile }, "build")`. Vite resolves an unset or relative `root` from `process.cwd()`. The LSP cwd can be another folder of a multi-root workspace. Plugins such as TanStack Start then read files from the wrong project, and the config fails to load.

This PR uses `resolveConfigFromFile()` from `vite-plus` 1.5.0 (voidzero-dev/vite-plus#3249). It resolves an unset or relative `root` from the config file's directory and keeps the user's `root`.

Assume the cwd is `/work/editor` and the config is `/repo/vite.config.ts`:

| Config `root` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unset | `/work/editor` | `/repo` |
| `"app"` | `/work/editor/app` | `/repo/app` |
| `"/srv/site"` | `/srv/site` | `/srv/site` |

- If the installed `vite-plus` does not export `resolveConfigFromFile` (older than 1.5.0), the loader falls back to `resolveConfig()` and keeps the old cwd-based behavior. The optional peer range is `"vite-plus": "*"`, so older versions can still occur.
- The `vite-plus` catalog moves to 1.5.0.
- A scoped override `vite-plus>vite: npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@1.5.0` keeps the Vite+ core for `vite-plus`. The global `vite` override replaced the core with upstream Vite, which ignores the internal option that `resolveConfigFromFile` uses. Keep this override in sync with the `vite-plus` catalog version.
- The Oxfmt CLI output normalizer now matches the shorter diagnostic format that the Vite+ core prints.
…(truncated)

fix(jsdoc): handle every line terminators as newline
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
`oxc_parser` normalizes line endings in template literals (their raw strings), but not in comments.
So a `Comment`, and the JSDoc in it, may contain non-LF line endings such as CR.

The problem: `oxc_jsdoc` split lines and tags only on `\n`, and treated `\r` as whitespace.
A JSDoc comment with lone CR line endings was read as a single line, so every tag after the first was absorbed into the previous tag's description.

This PR uses the existing `oxc_syntax::line_terminator` APIs, so every line terminator breaks a line properly.

Impact:

- oxlint: the jsdoc rules reported wrongly on files with lone CR line endings (e.g. a tag after the first one was missed)
- oxfmt: the JSDoc fixtures of `conformance:fixture` no longer differ on their CR variant

prs.title: test(formatter_tests): check CRLF and BOM variants in fixture harness
fix(formatter/jsdoc): handle every line terminator in multi-line JSDoc types
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Following the previous PR, the JSDoc formatter still detected multi-line types on `\n` only.
With lone CR line endings, their `*` line prefixes were kept and read as the `*` (any) type (`{{ any failed?: ..., any }}`).

Now, `tests/jsdoc.rs` also runs every fixture with LF, CRLF and CR.

prs.title: fix(formatter/jsdoc): strip `*` prefixes from multiline default value
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
A multi-line `[name=default]` (from `JSDocTagTypeNamePart::raw()`) kept its `*` line prefixes, so they were doubled on output, and with CR / CRLF a raw `\r` reached the printer (a debug panic).

- Strip the prefixes with `strip_jsdoc_star_prefixes()` and keep the lines as written
- Upstream drops the name and description here, recorded in `upstream-jsdoc-bugs.md#15`

feat(linter/promise/prefer-catch): implement suggestion
prs.author: baevm
prs.body:
This PR implements a suggestion for `promise/prefer-catch` rule, issue #4655.

Suggestion is only for `prom.then(undefined, fn2)` \ `prom.then(null, fn2)` cases. Other cases are reported without a suggestion, because rewriting `then(a, b)` as `catch(b).then(a)` or `then(a).catch(b)` changes behavior. Upstream has an open issue about this: https://github.com/eslint-community/eslint-plugin-promise/issues/613.

I also changed matcher from `ExpressionStatement` to `CallExpression`, because this rule missed a bunch of cases that upstream reports ([playground](https://playground.oxc.rs/?t=ir&lintRules=promise%2Fprefer-catch&options=%7B%22run%22%3A%7B%22lint%22%3Atrue%2C%22formatter%22%3Afalse%2C%22transform%22%3Afalse%2C%22isolatedDeclarations%22%3Afalse%2C%22whitespace%22%3Afalse%2C%22mangle%22%3Afalse%2C%22mangleProps%22%3Afalse%2C%22compress%22%3Afalse%2C%22scope%22%3Atrue%2C%22symbol%22%3Atrue%2C%22cfg%22%3Afalse%7D%2C%22parser%22%3A%7B%22extension%22%3A%22tsx%22%2C%22allowReturnOutsideFunction%22%3Atrue%2C%22preserveParens%22%3Atrue%2C%22allowV8Intrinsics%22%3Atrue%2C%22semanticErrors%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22linter%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22formatter%22%3A%7B%22useTabs%22%3Afalse%2C%22tabWidth%22%3A2%2C%22endOfLine%22%3A%22lf%22%2C%22printWidth%22%3A80%2C%22singleQuote%22%3Afalse%2C%22jsxSingleQuote%22%3Afalse%2C%22quoteProps%22%3A%22as-needed%22%2C%22trailingComma%22%3A%22all%22%2C%22semi%22%3Atrue%2C%22arrowParens%22%3A%22always%22%2C%22bracketSpacing%22%3Atrue%2C%22bracketSameLine%22%3Afa
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-restricted-imports): report re-exported imports once
prs.author: RamyAkin
prs.body:
`import { z } from 'zod'; export { z };` now reports the restricted import once. The module record represents the local re-export with an indirect export entry that copies the import's statement span, name, and type status. Skip that entry because the import has already been checked. A separate `export { z } from 'zod'` statement still receives its own report.

Build the import-statement span set once and share it between side-effect import checks and re-export de-duplication. Regression tests cover named, renamed, repeated, and default re-exports, path and pattern restrictions, and `allowTypeImports`.

Validation: `just lint -p oxc_linter`, `just test -p oxc_linter`, and `cargo fmt --check -p oxc_linter` pass after rebasing onto `origin/main`.

Fixes #28781

AI disclosure: Claude Code assisted with the original fix and tests; Codex assisted with review and follow-up edits.

prs.title: fix(linter/disable-directives): preserve separators and disable spans
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Unused-directive fixes in the LSP and partial loaders could join adjacent tokens or remove line breaks that affect automatic semicolon insertion. Paired directives also retained the matching enable comment's spans, so a fix could remove the enable and extend suppression.

Replace inline comments with a space while preserving embedded line terminators, and retain the original disable spans when closing intervals. Adds regressions for both bugs, which reproduce on main.

Prerequisite for #27698.

prs.title: fix(linter): remove unused `oxlint-disable` directives with `--fix`
prs.author: rtsao
prs.body:
Fixes #22420

- Apply unused directive fixes after linting, skipping files that other fixes already changed
- Make `oxlint-disable` directive removals a safe fix since only oxlint reads them (and JS plugins now run in both the CLI and LSP). Removal of `eslint-disable` comments remains a suggestion per #17522

AI disclosure: code authored with AI tools. I reviewed the changes and opened the PR myself

prs.title: fix(linter/react/exhaustive-deps): suggest dependency removals
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Removing `ref.current` or outer-scope dependencies can change when an effect runs. Mark these removals as dangerous suggestions so plain `--fix` preserves the dependency array and applying them requires `--fix-dangerously`.

Addresses the plain `--fix` behavior in #28884. Regression tests cover both reported cases and verify that only dangerous suggestions apply the removals.

feat(lexer): add more methods to `Vec128`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Where `Vec256` has a method which the Neon implementation performs in 2 halves, define that method on `Vec128` instead, and the `Vec256` method delegates to it for each half, with safe code. e.g.:

```rust
// Vec256::shl_u16 (Neon)
let (low, high) = self.into_halves();
Self::from_halves(low.shl_u16::<BITS>(), high.shl_u16::<BITS>())
```

This shortens code and makes it more readable. It also makes these methods available on `Vec128` as well, which may come in useful later.

prs.author: camc314

Skip object-destructuring fixes when replacing a declarator would discard comments, while retaining the diagnostic. Keep fixes that preserve comments inside the copied receiver or outside the replacement, with regression coverage for static and computed member access and parentheses.

prs.title: fix(linter/import/no-anonymous-default-export): report parenthesized exports
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Strip parentheses before checking default-export expressions so arrays, arrows, objects, calls, constructors and literals receive the same diagnostics as their unparenthesized forms. Preserve eslint-plugin-import behavior for function/class expressions and TypeScript wrappers, with regression coverage for those boundaries and allow options.

Fixes #28980

prs.title: fix(cfg): skip labeled contexts for unlabeled jumps
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Unlabeled jumps must skip labeled CFG contexts and target the enclosing loop or switch. Previously, an unlabeled `break` inside a labeled block could make `no-unreachable` miss code after the block and incorrectly flag reachable code after the loop.

Keep named-label resolution unchanged and add CFG and linter regressions for loop, switch, labeled-break, and continue behavior.

Fixes #28947

prs.title: fix(ecmascript): round nondecimal strings to numbers once
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Nondecimal `StringToNumber` accumulated digits in `f64`, losing low bits before the final rounding. For example, `"0x10000000000000801"` rounded to `2^64` instead of `2^64 + 4096`.

Retain an integer significand and sticky bit, then round once and scale by a power of two. Continue validating trailing digits after overflow. Regression tests cover binary, octal, and hexadecimal rounding boundaries, distant sticky bits, leading zeros, overflow, and invalid suffixes.

prs.title: fix(ecmascript): reject signs after nondecimal prefixes
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
`StringToNumber` accepted strings such as `"0x+1"`, `"0b+1"`, and `"0o+1"` as `1` because `u32::from_str_radix` permits a leading `+`. ECMAScript requires these strings to convert to `NaN`.

Reject signs immediately after nondecimal prefixes before parsing. Regression coverage includes uppercase prefixes, signs before and after prefixes, surrounding whitespace, both parsing paths, and `JSStr`, with signed decimal and Infinity controls.

Fixes #29035.

feat(lexer): runtime CPU feature set detection
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Switch `oxc_lexer` from choosing SIMD/generic implementation at build time to detecting the CPU's features at runtime.

Previously the AVX2 implementation was only used if the crate was compiled with `avx2`, `bmi2` and `popcnt` enabled (e.g. `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`). None of them is in the x86_64 baseline, so a normal build always used the generic implementation, even on CPUs which support AVX2.

After this PR, on x86_64:

- `DynCpu::detect` checks the CPU's features with `is_x86_feature_detected!`.
- The result is cached in a static `AtomicI8`, which holds the discriminant of the detected `DynCpu`, or -1 if it's not been detected yet.
- The fast path (already detected) is a single byte load and a sign check (very predictable branch).
- The actual check is in a `#[cold]`, `#[inline(never)]` function, which uses relaxed atomics and no locks. If threads race, each checks the CPU and stores the same value. Unlike with a `OnceLock`, no thread ever blocks or sleeps.

On aarch64, Neon is still selected at compile time. Neon is enabled by default at compile time on all aarch64 targets that support `std`. We do still support uncommon platforms which don't support Neon, and also disabling it with `-C target-feature=-neon` (breaks the target's float ABI, so seems highly unlikely anyone would want to do this). Either way, whether Neon is available or not can be detected at compile time.

On CI's x86_64 machines, which all support AVX2, normal builds now run the AVX2 implementation, no
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(lexer): do not include generic code in binary when compiled with AVX2 enabled
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Continuation of #28829.

When `oxc_lexer` is compiled with `avx2`, `bmi2` and `popcnt` enabled (e.g. `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`), the CPU is guaranteed to support AVX2, so the generic implementation can never run.

Make `Generic` uninhabited in that configuration, the same as it already is on aarch64 with Neon enabled.

- `Generic`'s field is `Never` when all 3 features are enabled at compile time.
- `BASELINE` is `Avx2`, instead of `Generic`. So all the crate's code (including cold paths and disambiguation's Level 3) is compiled for AVX2.
- `DynCpu::detect` returns static `Avx2` value without any branch or `is_x86_feature_detected!`.
- `#[cpu_multiversion]` macro treats `Generic` as uninhabited, so its `__generic` entry points start with `unreachable!()`.
- The compiler removes all the generic code from the binary.

When compiled with `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`, the crate shrinks from roughly 61k to 38k instructions.

Standard x86_64 build, and aarch64 builds are unaffected.

prs.title: feat(lexer): do not include Neon code in binary when compiled with Neon disabled on aarch64
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Continuation of #28829.

On aarch64 with Neon disabled at compile time (`-C target-feature=-neon`), there's no runtime check for Neon, so a `Neon` value is never created, and the Neon code can never run. But `Neon` was still inhabited, so the compiler couldn't know that, and kept all the Neon code in the binary.

In that configuration, make `Neon` uninhabited, and alter `#[cpu_multiversion]` macro so compiler removes all the Neon code from the binary.

Compiling the crate for aarch64 without Neon would be a very weird thing to do, so this is more for completeness and symmetry with the x86_64 setup, than for practical gain.

Every configuration now has exactly one CPU feature set, except x86_64 without AVX2 enabled at compile time, which has 2, and uses runtime feature detection.

This change also allows simplifying the `cpu` module, removing some code.

Builds for all other platforms/configurations are unaffected.
